liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (2 reviews): Jerry flubbed the opening lyrics of Bertha but grew stronger through the night; Brent's harmonies on Bertha were spine-tingling [22][27]
- **El Paso** (2 reviews): Weir was lit by a shining blue light during El Paso, which the listener found majestic; El Paso was a great surprise in the first set [20][22]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Opening with Greatest Story into Bertha, then Jackaroe and El Paso, made a well-played, solid first set [21]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Crazy Fingers was practically perfect [27]

## Setlist highlights

- **El Paso**: back after 162 archived shows (725 days) [32]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-04-03.nak300.pasternak.andrewf.89791.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 150 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd1989-04-03.nak300.bleich.sirmick.96796.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 150 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Vocals distort near the end of Bertha, and Walkin' Blues has a small tape problem around 3:17 [2]
- **gd89-04-03.beyerM88.connor.29758.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 23 songs; 133 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Overall sound quality of this recording is slightly below average [27]
- **gd1989-04-03.147893.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min [8]
- **gd89-04-03.sbd.harrel.7507.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 142 min; rated 3.92/5 by 13 [18]. Said about its sound: Pure soundboard that sounds far better than the previous night; fades in during the first verse of Greatest Story; Slight digital static appears around the one-minute mark of Greatest Story [24]

## Around the show

- The show closed with a double encore [23]
- After the previous night's disasters, a cloud hung over the show, with heavy police presence in Pennsylvania [30]
- Rumor said the band was angry about people crashing the gates the night before [30]
- After the previous night's disasters, a cloud hung over the show, with heavy police presence in Pennsylvania [31]
- Rumor said the band was angry about people crashing the gates the night before [31]
- The listener says the first night gets the raves, but preferred Weir's work on this night [20]
- Far more mellow and easy-going than the first night, with unusual song choices and placements [23]
- Good show but not quite as strong as the night before [30]
- Good show but not quite as strong as the night before [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-04-03.nak300.pasternak.andrewf.89791.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jon Pasternak; transferred by Andrew F; source: Nakamichi CM300/CP4's > Marantz PMD-420, front row of OTS. [1]. Also: A 4:29 patch from ShnID 29758 covers Drums (4:02) and Space (1:07) [1]
- **gd1989-04-03.nak300.bleich.sirmick.96796.sbeok.flac16**: taped by John Bleich; transferred by SIRMick; source: Nakamichi 300 shotguns > Sony WM-D6 > mac [2]. Also: Taped with Nakamichi CM300/CP4 microphones into a Marantz PMD-420; masters were lent by John; Tape flips after Built to Last and in Drums; the Drums gap is patched from shnid 89791 [2]
- **gd89-04-03.beyerM88.connor.29758.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB(11th Row)>Beyer Dynamic M88's>Sony TCD5M(CM)>Nak DR-10 (Playback)>Midiman Flying Cow 24bit/48kHz A/D>RME Digi96/8>Steinberg's Wavelab 3.0 (bit resolution &… [3]
- **gd1989-04-03.147893.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [8]. Also: Soundboard recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; Charlie Miller handled transfers and mastering, using two sets of masters [8]
- **gd89-04-03.sbd.harrel.7507.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > PCM (analog output) > D > D > CDR [18]
